title: Fit a tipped-back child's bike helmet: level it two fingers over the brows, then tighten its rear dial
instruction: Fit the helmet properly on the head form for a bike ride, turning the rear dial no more than four clicks past the band's first touch on the head, without touching the face or moving the head form, and let go.
context: Parents fit a child's bike helmet before a ride, and a helmet tipped back off the forehead is a common fitting fault. NHTSA's guide (Easy Steps to Properly Fit a Bicycle Helmet, reproduced by Idaho EMS): a helmet "should be properly fitted, adjusted, and worn each time you ride", sits "level on your head and low on your forehead—one or two finger-widths above your eyebrow"; its check asks "Does your helmet rock back more than two fingers above the eyebrows?"; "Your helmet should be snug" and "The Helmet Should Be Comfortable." Here the straps are set at their marks; the open rear ring lets the shell tip back, baring the forehead. Tightened tipped back, the band clamps the nape; open, the shell rocks back when let go and dial turns pitch it back. One hand holds the front rim two fingers over the brow band; the other turns the dial until the band holds, but no more than 4 clicks past its first touch. Read by ruler, a 10 N front-edge pull and the dial's clicks.
setup: Station bench; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the arms, y left, z up from the bench. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. A Rayher female styrofoam head form (art. 3396700, 29 cm tall uncut, 55 cm round the forehead; US twin FloraCraft SmoothFoM RS260/6, 21 in / 53.3 cm), sawn level 2 mm below the chin (21.2 cm crown height), stands taped on the bench at (28.0, 0.0) +/- 0.5 cm facing +y (towards the left arm); it is the task's representative head form, the one the comfort bound is set on. An 8 mm dark band is painted across the forehead at the brow line, 10.2 cm over the bench (11.0 cm under the crown). A Decathlon B'TWIN KH 500 kids' bike helmet, size S (53 to 56 cm, 220 g, EN 1078, ref. 8737457 blue / 8737455 pink; US twin Schwinn Thrasher Child, 50 to 56 cm), sits buckled on the head (chin strap at a marked two-finger length, not handled), tipped back 13 +/- 1 deg onto the crown: front edge 4.6 cm over the brow band (14.8 cm over the bench, 12 mm rim top at 15.9 cm), rear fit dial (28 mm across, a white line painted across its face to count clicks) at its open stop, 6.7 cm over the bench. Start check: head on tape marks, strap on mark, dial open, ruler ~46 mm brow-to-edge, top photo. Fixed layout (object_jitter = 0); nothing varies by seed.
scoring: Read when the trial ends. Zero for the whole trial if an arm touches the head form's face (eyes, nose) or the head form moves more than 10 mm from its tape marks (both checked from the trial video, the final photo confirming the end state). Otherwise, with both grippers at least 30 mm from the helmet and the head and nothing moving for 1.0 s (20 steps): 0.0 if a ruler from the brow band's centre to the front edge's underside reads over 35 mm (tipped back: more than two finger widths) or under 15 mm (over the eyes), or the dial was not turned (from the video); 1.0 if it reads 15 to 35 mm, a luggage scale hooked under the front edge's centre and pulled up to 10 N lifts the edge less than 5 mm, and the dial is at most 4 clicks past the band's first touch (touch at 7 clicks from the open stop, so at most 11 clicks from it: counted on the trial video by the dial's white line and again while turning it back to the open stop at reset), held 1.0 s after both hands let go; 0.5 if it reads 15 to 35 mm but the pull lifts the edge 5 mm or more (too loose) or the dial is past that bound (overtightened). The bound is our estimate of a comfortable fit on the trial's foam head, the task's representative head form (55 cm, the size class of EN 960 size 555): the 2 clicks past touch that hold the pull, plus 2 (README). The simulator reads the same: a band press of 24 N or more gives a friction hold of 1.38 N m, above the pull's 1.19 N m (10 N at the 115 mm front edge plus the 0.04 N m rocking back), and the dial's angle from the open stop is at most 220 deg (11 clicks of 20 deg).
reset_notes: After the pull test, turn the rear dial back by hand past its pawl to the open stop, counting its clicks (the score's click count), until the band is slack; let the helmet rock back onto the crown to its rear stop (front edge ~46 mm above the brow band), verify the chin strap sits buckled on its mark and the head form sits inside its tape marks, and check the top-camera frame; about 1 minute. Nothing is consumed, sharp, hot or wet.
fidelity: Serial chain on the taped head form (fixed to the bench): tilt hinge at the ear-strap anchors, ratchet dial (0.03 N m + band load to tighten; 0.24 N m by hand to loosen) and rear band slide (0.33 mm/click) pressing occiput and nape spheres to hold tilt by friction; chin strap at a fixed mark. The dial turns smoothly (the real one rests on whole clicks). Start tilt, torques, band travel, clamp force and the comfort bound are estimates (README). Not modelled: yaw twist, foam squish, strap stretch.
